queer_characters.name: Leo
queer_characters.notes: Leo's intimacy with Remi is queer-coded but never explicitly labeled; the film centers on how societal assumptions read their bond as romantic. Any queer identity is a reading of subtext, not stated in text.
queer_characters.contest_notes: Director Dhont explicitly stated the film 'is not about their sexuality' and deliberately avoids confirming or denying the boys' orientation. Some read Leo as queer/questioning; the text supports neither confirmation nor denial.

queer_characters.name: Remi
queer_characters.notes: Remi's deep intimacy with Leo is queer-coded; his death follows homophobic social pressure. No explicit orientation is stated in the film.
queer_characters.contest_notes: The film deliberately avoids labeling Remi's sexuality; Dhont framed the story as about intimacy and how it is perceived rather than confirmed queerness.

contributor_notes: Per the source, Close deliberately avoids explicit queer labeling; both boys are queer-coded rather than confirmed queer, so all identity tags are marked 'inferred' and contested. The tragic-queer and bury-your-gays tropes are noted because a queer-coded character (Remi) dies by suicide following homophobic pressure, but a maintainer should weigh that against Dhont's stated intent that the film transcends queer experience alone. No subtitle/audio info was provided in the source. Please review contested flags carefully.
